successCriteria.description: The four shared enums are defined and exported from `src/shared/types/index.ts`: `LeaveRequestStatus` (DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED), `LeaveType` (annual, sick, emergency, unpaid, maternity, paternity), `BalanceStatus` (ACTIVE, EXHAUSTED, CLOSED), `EmploymentStatus` (ACTIVE, INACTIVE, TERMINATED).
The `BaseEntity` interface is defined and exported from `src/shared/types/index.ts` with exactly the fields `id: string`, `createdAt: Date`, `updatedAt: Date`.

The `AuditRecord` entity is defined in `src/modules/audit/audit.model.ts` with the exact canonical fields: `id: string`, `entityType: string`, `entityId: string`, `action: string`, `oldValues: Record<string, unknown> | null`, `newValues: Record<string, unknown> | null`, `performedBy: string`, `performedAt: Date`, `ipAddress: string | undefined`, `userAgent: string | undefined`, `createdAt: Date`. It does NOT extend `BaseEntity` (no `updatedAt` field — immutable audit log).

`IAuditRepository` interface is defined in `src/modules/audit/audit.repository.interface.ts` with methods `create(record: AuditRecord): Promise<AuditRecord>` and `findByEntity(entityType: string, entityId: string): Promise<AuditRecord[]>`.

`IAuditService` interface is defined in `src/modules/audit/audit.service.interface.ts` with a single `record` method accepting params: `entityType`, `entityId`, `action`, optional `oldValues`/`newValues` (both `Record<string, unknown> | null | undefined`), `performedBy`, optional `ipAddress`/`userAgent`, and returning `Promise<AuditRecord>`.

`AuditService` class implements `IAuditService` and receives `IAuditRepository` via constructor injection. Its `record` method constructs an `AuditRecord` with `id` generated via `crypto.randomUUID()`, `performedAt` set to `new Date()`, `createdAt` set to `new Date()`, and delegates to `repository.create(record)`, returning the result.

Jest unit test at `tests/unit/modules/audit/audit.service.test.ts` mocks `IAuditRepository` and verifies: (a) `record()` constructs the `AuditRecord` with a UUID id, correct `performedAt`/`createdAt` timestamps, and all passed-through fields; (b) `record()` calls `repository.create` exactly once with the constructed record; (c) `record()` returns the value returned by `repository.create`.

constraints: No `any` type anywhere — use `unknown` with type guards. The `oldValues` and `newValues` fields must use `Record<string, unknown>`, not `any`. (HARNESS.json constraint: no-any)

All database access must go through the repository pattern. The concrete `IAuditRepository` implementation (Knex/Postgres) is deferred to a later phase; this phase defines only the interface. (GP-001, HARNESS.json constraint: no-direct-db-outside-repository)
Strict TypeScript: `strict: true` in tsconfig — no implicit any, strict null checks. All nullable/optional fields must be explicitly typed as `| null` or `| undefined` as specified.
outOfScope: Concrete `IAuditRepository` implementation (Knex/Postgres) — deferred to a later phase. Only the interface is defined now.
Fastify routes, controllers, or HTTP endpoints for the audit module — this phase is foundation types and service layer only.

entityInvariants.invariant: AuditRecord is immutable after creation — it has no `updatedAt` field and does not extend `BaseEntity`. Once written, an audit record must never be modified or deleted.

Every domain entity that supports updates (Employee, LeaveRequest, LeavePolicy, LeaveBalance) must extend `BaseEntity`, which guarantees `id: string`, `createdAt: Date`, and `updatedAt: Date`. AuditRecord is the sole exception — it is immutable and does not extend BaseEntity.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: No auth enforcement at this layer — the caller (service or controller) is responsible for providing the correct `performedBy` identity. The audit service records whatever identity it receives.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Must propagate errors from the underlying repository (e.g. connection failures) without swallowing them. Must not throw for missing optional fields — `oldValues`, `newValues`, `ipAddress`, `userAgent` are all optional and may be `undefined` or `null`.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: No auth — repository is a pure data-access interface.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Must return the created `AuditRecord` (with any server-generated defaults applied). Must reject on persistence failure.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: No auth — repository is a pure data-access interface.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns an array (empty if no records found — never null). Must reject on query failure.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The `AuditRecord` entity must match the canonical field list in `.gestalt/architecture/reconciled.json` exactly: `id`, `entityType`, `entityId`, `action`, `oldValues`, `newValues`, `performedBy`, `performedAt`, `ipAddress`, `userAgent`, `createdAt`. No extra fields, no missing fields.

The four enums (`LeaveRequestStatus`, `LeaveType`, `BalanceStatus`, `EmploymentStatus`) must match the values declared in `.gestalt/architecture/reconciled.json` under the `shared-types` module. No extra enum members, no missing members.

Module structure must follow the existing pattern established by `src/modules/uptime/` and `src/modules/status/`: a model file, a service interface file, a service implementation file, and a barrel `index.ts`. The audit module adds a repository interface file (`audit.repository.interface.ts`) which is a new pattern for this project but required by GP-001.

integrationPoints.why: All downstream modules (employee, leave-policy, leave-balance, leave-request) import enums and BaseEntity from here. The audit module's audit.model.ts imports BaseEntity from here.
